notes.title: Visual enhancements and added voiceover
notes.content:
[h1]Hello Detectives![/h1]

After almost exactly one month, we're back with another update. This time we're bringing [b]two major improvements[/b] to Timeshift Detective which we're happy to announce.

First, we [b]freshened up the visual style[/b] a bit, overhauling how we utilize lighting and colors to create a more [b]atmospheric[/b] and [b]moody environment[/b].
You can see some before and after examples of the visual update below.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44742517/7c088a6c5ac39be976fbb7bb9227876e619878e2.gif[/img]

Second, we added a full [b]voiceover[/b] to each and every dialogue or monologue in the game. This lends some [b]more personality[/b] to our characters and reduces the amount of mandatory reading for those of you less inclined to do so. Unfortunately, we can't show you that in a gif. But hopefully you won't have to wait too long before we can present you some video content including audio bits!

[h2]But wait, there is more:[/h2]
[list]
[*] Made Bernstein's apartment more chaotic
[*] Added the Mysteries UI, making it easier to remember unsolved mysteries
[*] Added the option to skip cutscenes and previously heard dialogues
[*] Added a contextual marker to questions in the notebook which indicates an unresolved confrontation
[*] A location's name is now shown after entering it
[*] The pause menu now uses regular gameplay as its background
[*] Tweaked the texts of some dialogues
[*] Various bugfixes
[/list]
